title: Porous media, momentum sources, MRF (rotating frame) source terms
acceptance: Packed-bed Ergun pressure drop and rotating channel tests pass
note: Wave 9. Acceptance met, scope partial. Delivered: rcfd-fv sources.rs (Darcy-Forchheimer porous sink in the superficial-velocity form, Ergun coefficients 1/K = 150 (1-e)^2/(e^3 d^2), C2 = 3.5 (1-e)/(e^3 d); relative-velocity rotating frame with analytic centrifugal and lagged Coriolis accelerations as balanced-force BodyForce terms; constant acceleration), rcfd-api sources.rs and settings sources.<name> (type porous | rotating_frame | acceleration; zone all | box | cell_zone; steady simple/simplec only, other algorithms are a located diagnostic; docs/case-schema.md; cases/packed_bed, cases/rotating_channel). Ergun constants checked against a secondary source (neutrium.net, Manchester packed-bed page; Ergun 1952 itself not accessed). Checks fixed before running (rcfd-api tests/sources.rs, nu = 1.5e-5, bed e = 0.4, d = 5 mm, U = 0.15 m/s, 40x8 cells): packed-bed kinematic pressure gradient between 30 % and 70 % of the bed 149.7666 vs Ergun 149.7656 (+0.001 %, limit 1 %; the viscous and inertial terms are 51 %/49 % of it); direct Darcy-Forchheimer input gives the same field to 1e-9; a porous box zone over the middle half gives 149.7965 inside (+0.02 %) and -0.041 outside (0.03 % of Ergun, limit 1 %). Spanwise-rotating laminar channel (Omega = 2, nu = 0.1, g = 1, 4x40 cells, Coriolis only): profile error 0.062 % of the centre-line velocity (limit 1 %), transverse pressure difference -3.3371 vs -2 Omega times the integral of the parabola -3.3302 (+0.21 %, limit 1 %). NOT met: fluid at rest in a rotating frame (closed 1 m box, Coriolis + centrifugal, nu = 0.05, Omega = 3): the pre-fixed criterion was spurious speed < 1e-3 Omega R_max and pressure error < 1 % of the range; measured 5.2e-3 and 1.62 % on 24x24, 1.3e-3 and 0.80 % on 48x48 (speed falls with order 2.0, pressure with order 1.0); cause: next to walls the Green-Gauss cell gradient of a curved pressure field differs from the cell-centre force by O(h), the same wall effect as the rest state of F-050 (an attempt to change the wall pressure extrapolation did not help and was reverted). The cross-stream velocity of the rotating channel is 1.4e-5 of the centre-line speed for the same reason. The normalised momentum residual cannot be used as a stop criterion for these uniform or linear solutions (its normalisation vanishes); the tests check stationarity instead. Not done (reason for partial): MRF zone interface (frozen-rotor absolute/relative velocity conversion between a rotating and a stationary zone needs the non-conformal interface of F-114), transient PISO/PIMPLE support, porosity-weighted (physical-velocity) formulation, anisotropic/directional resistance, porous jump (F-113).

title: Coupled pressure-velocity solver (block-coupled) with AMG
acceptance: Cavity converges in fewer outer iterations than SIMPLE; documented
note: Block-coupled solver (rcfd-fv coupled.rs, solver.algorithm = "coupled"): (u,v[,w],p) in one system per Picard iteration, implicit Green-Gauss pressure gradient, implicit Rhie-Chow continuity rows, GMRES(40) with ILU(0) momentum blocks and one AMG V-cycle on the approximate pressure Schur complement (AMG is used on the pressure block only, not on the full interleaved system). Measured (checks fixed beforehand: F-028 cavity Re 100, 40x40, linearUpwind; shared measure = first outer iteration after which the velocity stays within 1e-5 U_lid of the solver's own converged state, same function for both solvers; coupled must pass the unchanged Ghia gate 0.02 U_lid for u and v): coupled alpha_u 0.9 settles at 165 outer iterations (270 total, 3060 GMRES iterations), SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9 at 167 (273), classic SIMPLE alpha_u 0.7 at 610 (917); Ghia max error u 0.00277, v 0.00855 (SIMPLEC identical, limit 0.02). Acceptance (fewer outer iterations than SIMPLE) met against SIMPLE (165 vs 610), but at equal relaxation the coupled solver needs the same number of Picard iterations as SIMPLEC (the count is set by the momentum under-relaxation, not the coupling); its advantage is stability at stronger relaxation: alpha_u 0.95 settles at 83, 0.98 at 38 outer iterations versus SIMPLEC best 97 (0.95; 249 at 0.98). Wall time is worse: 1.9 s at 0.98 versus 0.6 s for SIMPLEC at 0.95 (ILU/AMG rebuilt each iteration, unoptimised); AMG-less Jacobi Schur block needs 2 to 5 times more GMRES iterations (e.g. 14181 vs 3060 at alpha_u 0.9). Scope limits (hence partial): closed domains with the velocity prescribed on every boundary, laminar, no body force, sources, energy, turbulence, non-orthogonal correction or periodic patches (all rejected with located diagnostics); transient coupled solve and open boundaries not done.

title: Wall distance calculation and standard wall functions
acceptance: y+ and wall distance verified on channel mesh; log law recovered in developed flow
note: Wave 5. rcfd-turb: wall_distance (exact Euclidean distance from each cell centre to the nearest wall face, faces split into triangle fans, closest-point test per Ericson, bounding-box pruning; no Poisson/PDE method), WallConstants (kappa 0.41, E 9.8, Cmu 0.09; Launder and Spalding 1974 equilibrium log law with the viscous-sublayer switch at the y+ intersection, 11.5 for these constants), u_tau from the first-cell velocity by Newton iteration, wall eddy viscosity from velocity (nu_t,w = u_tau^2 y/u_P - nu) and from k (nu_t,w = nu (y* kappa / ln(E y*) - 1), y* = Cmu^1/4 sqrt(k) y / nu), wall_y_plus, effective_viscosity (face viscosity for SimpleSolver.nu_face with wall-function values on wall faces) and a Prandtl mixing-length closure (l = kappa d) with the log-law value kappa y u_tau in wall cells. Verification (rcfd-turb tests): wall distance equals min(y, 2h-y) to 1e-13 on uniform and graded channel meshes and equals x for a side wall; triangle distance covers face/edge/vertex regions. Periodic channel at Re_tau = 395 (h = 1, u_tau = 1 imposed through the body force, nu = 1/395), mixing-length interior plus wall functions, ny = 8/12/16 (first-cell y+ = 49.4/32.9/24.7): reported y+ equals y u_tau/nu within 0.5%; wall shear from the wall function equals the imposed 1 within 2e-3 (momentum balance); first-cell u+ on the log law; interior profile vs the exact solution of the mixing-length stress balance (nu + l^2 S) S = 1 - y/h: max deviation 2.1% / 2.3% / 2.4% (the offset is the second-order stencil error across the log layer between the first two cells of a uniform mesh, centre distances 1:3, and does not shrink with ny; test tolerance 3%). Caveats: the log-law is recovered with a mixing-length interior closure, not yet with k-epsilon (F-042); a comparison with DNS is left to F-042. Convergence of this stiff diffusion-dominated flow needed the new opt-in SimpleSettings.h_from_solution (H operator from the solved predictor as in classic SIMPLE; default off, ~6x faster here: the default Jacobi-like H needed >8000 iterations); the normalised momentum residual is meaningless for the identically zero v component (round-off noise), so the test converges on max velocity update < 1e-10. Wave 6b: the wall functions are reachable from the case schema through turbulence.model = k_epsilon (turbulence.wall_function = standard, kappa, e_wall), with the y_plus field/boundary value/report (type y_plus, statistic average|min|max) and the k, epsilon, nut, wall_distance fields in VTU output; the mixing-length closure is not selectable from the schema. Scalable wall functions and rough walls are not included.

title: k-epsilon family (standard, realizable, RNG) with scalable wall functions
acceptance: Channel Re_tau=395 mean profile within 10 percent of DNS; backward-facing-step reattachment within literature scatter
note: Wave 5, PARTIAL: channel criterion met, backward-facing-step criterion NOT attempted. rcfd-turb kepsilon.rs: KEpsilon with variants Standard (Launder-Spalding 1974), RNG (Yakhot-Orszag; C2* strain correction) and Realizable (Shih et al. 1995; variable Cmu, C1 = max(0.43, eta/(eta+5)), eps sink C2 eps^2/(k+sqrt(nu eps))), implicit-sink k and epsilon transport on the SIMPLE flux (rcfd-fv convection/laplacian), standard wall functions from F-040 (wall-cell epsilon fixed to Cmu^3/4 k^3/2/(kappa y), wall-shear production, wall-face nu_t from k), nu_t under-relaxed; library API only (nu_face() feeds SimpleSolver.nu_face; run with SimpleSettings.h_from_solution = true). Test tests/channel_kepsilon.rs: periodic channel Re_tau = 395 (h = 1, u_tau = 1 via body force, nu = 1/395), 4 x 14 uniform cells (first-cell y+ 28), converged (max update < 1e-9, nu_t change < 1e-8) in about 4500-4800 iterations. Centre-line U+ / bulk U+: Standard 20.69 (+2.9%) / 18.39 (+5.7%), RNG 21.14 (+5.2%) / 18.65 (+7.2%), Realizable 21.59 (+7.4%) / 18.93 (+8.8%) against DNS (Moser, Kim and Mansour 1999) 20.1 / 17.4 -- all within the 10% criterion; log-layer profile (20 < y+ < 150) within 10% of Reichardt's law (test asserts it; Standard 13.91 vs 13.37 at y+ 28, 16.63 vs 16.52 at y+ 85). CAVEATS: DNS numbers verified in wave 6a against the published MKM chan395.means (actual Re_tau 392.24: U_c+ = 20.13, U_b+ = 17.54, Re_b = 13764) and the RNG/realizable/standard constants verified against Fluent/OpenFOAM documentation (realizable A0 is 4.04 in Fluent, 4.0 in OpenFOAM); only the 14-cell mesh was run (no mesh study); the profile comparison beyond the log layer is only through the centre-line and bulk values; all three variants overpredict the velocity, Realizable the most. NOT DONE: backward-facing-step reattachment: the available step mesh generator has uniform spacing only and expansion ratio 2 does not match Driver and Seegmiller (1985, ER 1.125, xr/H about 6.26), the second-order BFS convergence problem found in F-106 at Re_h >= 200 is undiagnosed, and no reference-consistent case was set up, so no reattachment number is claimed. Wave 6b: wired into the case schema (rcfd-api turb.rs): turbulence.model = laminar | k_epsilon, turbulence.variant = standard | rng | realizable, wall_function, kappa, e_wall, convection, relax, relax_nut, k_initial/epsilon_initial or initial_intensity/initial_viscosity_ratio; inlet helpers per boundary (turbulence_spec = intensity_length | intensity_viscosity_ratio | values: k = 3/2 (I U)^2, epsilon = Cmu^3/4 k^3/2 / l or Cmu k^2/(ratio nu), checked in a test against the area average of the boundary k/epsilon); outputs k, epsilon, nut, y_plus, res_nut monitor. Validation errors with line numbers: transient algorithm, no wall patch, moving wall, energy equation, missing turbulence_length, inconsistent k/epsilon initial values, y_plus report on a non-wall patch. Tests (rcfd-api tests/physics_schema.rs): the periodic Re_tau 395 channel run through the settings tree equals the library run after 60 iterations to 1e-12 (u, k, nut; standard, RNG, realizable); converged run (4508 iterations in cases/channel/kepsilon_channel.toml, stopped by a y+ plateau because the relative momentum residual stalls near 5e-4) gives bulk U+ 18.389 (the library test value 18.39, +5.7% vs DNS 17.4), wall-cell y+ 27.733; cases/channel/kepsilon_inlet.toml runs through rcfd run and the service. Still no scalable wall functions, k-epsilon is steady-only, incompressible, without heat transfer, and the backward-facing step is still not attempted; multiple wall faces per cell use the nearest only. WAVE 6 UPDATE (supersedes the 'NOT DONE: backward-facing-step' item above; status stays PARTIAL because scalable wall functions and schema wiring are still missing). Step case: tests/step_kepsilon.rs (rcfd-turb, #[ignore], run in release), Driver and Seegmiller geometry via StepSpec::from_expansion_ratio(1.125) (inlet channel 8 h, step 1 h, l_in 5, l_out 40), graded mesh (backward_step_graded), standard wall functions, SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.8 linearUpwind momentum, upwind k/epsilon, Re_h = 37500. Measured reattachment x_r/h (last negative-to-positive sign change of u in the first cell row above the floor; 4000-5000 iterations), three meshes (5.1k / 10.6k / 23.8k cells; 3000 iterations on the coarse and fine meshes, 5000 on the medium one): Standard 5.20 / 5.36 / 5.46, RNG 6.32 / 6.37 / 6.38, Realizable (medium mesh) 6.40, against Driver and Seegmiller 6.26 +- 0.10 (value from cases/backward_step/case.json; secondary sources checked this wave - NASA NPARC validation archive and the OpenFOAM verification docs built on the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource case - give 6.26 +- 0.10 for the zero-degree top wall, quoted there at Re_h = 36000, while case.json and the runs use 37500) and the 5.5-7 RANS scatter band in that file: RNG and Realizable are inside the scatter band, 0.06-0.14 above the nominal 6.26 (RNG 6.32 on the coarsest mesh is inside the +-0.10 window, the finer meshes are 0.01-0.04 above it); Standard is 13-17 percent LOW, below the band on the two coarser meshes and 0.04 below it on the finest. So the 'within literature scatter' criterion is met by RNG/Realizable only. CAVEATS: the inlet is an approximation (1/7 power-law boundary layer thickness 1.5 h on both inlet-channel walls, 1 percent free-stream intensity, k and eps from a mixing-length estimate), not the measured D&S profile; the top wall is straight, which matches the zero-degree reference configuration; fixed outlet pressure at x/h = 40; the nu_t of the wall-adjacent cells on the viscous/log switch oscillates O(1) between iterations (max velocity update stalls at 3e-4 - 4e-3, 'nut change < 1e-6' never reached) although x_r is constant to 1e-5 on the medium and fine meshes (fine RNG: 6.37817 from iteration 1500 to 3000); k-epsilon constants/RNG/realizable forms still from memory; no schema wiring. docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md. WAVE 7 UPDATE (status stays PARTIAL: scalable wall functions are still not implemented and only RNG/Realizable are inside the step scatter band). The wall-cell oscillation reported above is DIAGNOSED AND FIXED: a top-N listing of the changing nu_t cells showed all of them wall-adjacent (step face and floor), i.e. the hard viscous/log switch of the wall function (epsilon jumps about 4x, production 0 to log-law). rcfd-turb now has WallTreatment { Switch (old), Hysteresis{band} (+-10 percent dead band, band 0.1), Smooth (default: epsilon_w = sqrt(eps_vis^2 + eps_log^2), compound form after Popovac and Hanjalic 2007, and log-law production times r^6/(1+r^6), r = y*/y*_lam) }, selectable as turbulence.wall_treatment = smooth | hysteresis | switch in the case schema. With the UNCHANGED criterion (max velocity update < 1e-7 and nu_t change < 1e-6) tests/step_kepsilon.rs now asserts convergence (hysteresis and smooth): medium mesh (24+160 x 40+20 cells) converges in 800-920 iterations (du 1e-8, dnut 1e-6) for Standard, RNG and Realizable; Switch never does (du 2e-4 - 1.7e-3, dnut 0.4 - 1.1). Measured x_r/H (target 6.26 +- 0.10 and the tolerances are unchanged), medium mesh: Switch 5.3583 / 6.3726 / 6.4042 (Standard / RNG / Realizable), Hysteresis 5.3581 / 6.3724 / 6.4043, Smooth 5.3594 / 6.3729 / 6.4015; fine mesh (36+240 x 60+30, Smooth, converged at about 1540-1570 iterations) 5.4599 / 6.3797 / 6.5063. The treatment moves x_r by less than 0.003, so the earlier numbers stand: RNG and Realizable are inside the 5.5-7 scatter band (0.11-0.25 above the nominal 6.26; RNG medium/fine 6.37/6.38 are 0.01-0.02 outside the +-0.10 window, Realizable 6.40-6.51 is 0.04-0.15 outside), Standard (5.36-5.46) is outside the band. Channel (tests/channel_kepsilon.rs, 10 percent assertions unchanged, all pass) shifts slightly with the smooth default: centre-line / bulk U+ Standard 20.742 (+3.2%) / 18.441 (+6.0%), RNG 21.193 (+5.4%) / 18.702 (+7.5%), Realizable 21.630 (+7.6%) / 18.973 (+9.0%, close to the 10 percent limit); U+ at y+ 28.2 13.957 vs Reichardt 13.372. Details: docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md.

title: k-omega SST (and BSL) with low-Re wall treatment
acceptance: Flat plate / BFS / NACA0012 validation passes; y+~1 meshes stable

To make buoyancy balance at walls the SIMPLE pressure condition on prescribed-velocity boundaries now extrapolates the wall pressure with the gradient that balances the body force (fixed-flux pressure); this only changes runs with a body force acting normal to a wall. Effect, measured on the de Vahl Davis cavity: Ra=1e4 n=40 Nu error +1.77% -> +0.02%, Ra=1e5 n=64 +2.98% -> +0.07%; stably stratified fluid at rest: spurious face flux 0.54 -> 8e-4 (forcing ~3e3). acceptance: Nozzle flow matches isentropic relations; choked mass flow within 1 percent
note: Wave 10. Acceptance met for the ideal gas, scope partial (the real-gas EOS interface is not wired into the pressure-based kernel; only the ideal-gas EOS is). Pressure-based compressible extension: rcfd-fv varden.rs (ADR 0005), fluid.density = ideal_gas, fluid.mode = compressible with a stagnation inlet. Checks written into the ADR before any run: quasi-1-D converging-duct (subsonic, throat Mach 0.3, 200x10 cells, linear upwind, SIMPLEC): column Mach error 7.3e-4 (limit 1.5e-2), p/p0 5.1e-5 (5e-3), T/T0 2.2e-5 (3e-3), mass flow vs the isentropic value -7.6e-4 at inlet and outlet (limit 1e-2), inlet/outlet equality 4.8e-13. Choked converging-diverging nozzle (240x12, exit Mach 1.854, supersonic branch, p_e/p0 = 0.1602): Mach error 9.2e-4 (limit 3e-2), p/p0 1.3e-3 (2e-2), choked mass flow vs A* p0 sqrt(gamma/(R T0)) (2/(gamma+1))^((gamma+1)/(2(gamma-1))) -4.05e-4 at inlet and outlet (acceptance limit 1 percent), in/out 2e-14. Deviation: the choked case needs under-relaxation 0.7/0.5/0.7 (defaults 0.9/1.0/0.9 diverged when the supersonic region forms) and a back-pressure continuation start-up (0.98 p0 to p_e in 40 stages of 100 iterations, then 6000 iterations at p_e); starting at the mean pressure diverged. These start-up choices were not registered, the tolerances were not changed. Isentropic and area-Mach relations are standard textbook formulae. The choked test is heavy (about 80 s release, #[ignore]). Caveats: steady and laminar only, no shock capturing beyond what the first/second-order upwind density gives (not tested), residual res_u floors at about 1e-5..1e-6 for the cavity and nozzle cases. API wiring test (nozzle_2d case file): mass flow in/out within 1e-6 and throat Mach 0.2997 vs 0.3 met; the registered residual target 1e-8 was NOT met (res_u 2.6e-5, res_p 6e-13 at 3000 iterations), so such runs stop at max_iterations unless convergence conditions are used.

title: Pseudo-transient (local time-stepping) steady solver option with automatic timescale selection
acceptance: Lid-driven cavity at Re 1000 and a backward-facing step converge with pseudo-transient where plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation; timescale factor and auto/local/physical modes selectable in the settings tree
note: P1. Gap: CFX convergence control (physical, local, auto timescale) and Fluent pseudo-transient controls both exist; improves robustness for phases 3-5. Partial (wave 5). Done: the SIMPLE/SIMPLEC pseudo-transient term (V/dt added to the momentum diagonal with explicit old-iterate source, before relaxation) was already in rcfd-fv simple.rs but untested and not exposed; now selectable in the settings tree: solver.pseudo_mode = off | auto (one global step factor*L/U_max) | local (per-cell dt = cfl*V/sum(0.5|phi|+nu*lap)) | physical (fixed dt), with solver.pseudo_cfl, solver.pseudo_dt and the timescale factor solver.pseudo_factor. Tests: rcfd-api case test runs all modes from the tree; rcfd-fv factor test (factor 0.4 on cfl 5 equals cfl 2). Measured, lid-driven cavity Re=1000, 32x32, linearUpwind (tests/pseudo.rs, release): plain SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9/0.95/1.0 diverge (no convergence in 5296/4154/3298 iterations, residual ~0.7, then non-finite); SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 converges in 1900 iterations; pseudo-transient with alpha_u = 1 (no momentum relaxation) converges to residual 1e-6 for local cfl 2 (1798), cfl 5 (1364), physical dt 0.05 (1918), 0.2 (1515) and auto (1532 iterations), all to the same steady state. Larger pseudo steps fail: local cfl >= 10 and physical dt 1 do not converge (residual ~0.6-0.7). 64x64 vanLeer: SIMPLEC 0.95 does not converge in 6000 its (residual 3.7e-2), pseudo local cfl 5 converges in 3996, SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 in 4552 (wave-5 exploration run, not a kept test). NOT met: the backward-facing step. With the project backward_step mesh (uniform inlet, expansion ratio 2, 16+80 x 8+8 cells; Re_h=400 vanLeer also 32+160 x 16+16) Re_h=100 converges with every variant (SIMPLE 646 its, pseudo cfl 5 571; kept as a light test) and Re_h=200/400 with second-order schemes (vanLeer, linearUpwind) does not converge with ANY variant, including plain SIMPLE 0.7/0.3, SIMPLEC 0.9 and all pseudo modes tried (residual stalls 0.05-0.5 or diverges); with first-order upwind Re_h=200 converges for all, Re_h=400 only for SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (1395 its). So the step case shows no pseudo-transient advantage and points to an unresolved robustness issue of second-order schemes on the step (corner/outlet) that was not diagnosed. Note: an earlier exploration table with 'res 0.00e0' entries was invalid (NaN fields); the test harness now treats non-finite fields as failure. Next: diagnose the step (outlet backflow treatment, limiter chatter at the corner, deferred-correction under-relaxation), then re-run the BFS comparison. Wave 6b: remaining solver settings of the library are now in the schema: solver.h_operator (default | from_solution | previous_iterate), p_ref_cell/p_ref_value, bulk_velocity/bulk_direction (mean-velocity driver), physics.body_force, momentum/pressure linear-solver tolerances and iteration caps, ddt_correction, and res_T/res_nut/res_rho are accepted convergence monitors; the pseudo-transient and energy settings were already exposed (see above) and are unchanged. Documented in rcfd/docs/case-schema.md. WAVE 6 UPDATE: the step failure is DIAGNOSED AND FIXED. Root cause: SimpleSettings.h_from_solution defaulted to false, i.e. H (and the Rhie-Chow flux) used the previous iterate instead of the solved momentum predictor, a Jacobi-like lagged iteration that is marginally unstable with second-order deferred correction (wave of O(1) amplitude, wavelength ~10 cells, growing toward the outlet; l_out 10 converged, l_out 14-20 did not; dx 0.5 and 0.125 converged, 0.25 did not; alpha 0.5/0.2 converged). Now default true (still false while a MeanVelocityDriver is active, whose gain assumes the lagged response). Evidence and tables: docs/bfs-convergence-findings.md. Measured after the fix: step (uniform inlet, ER 2, 16+80 x 8+8) Re_h = 200 linearUpwind SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 646 its; cavity Re = 1000 32x32 linearUpwind plain SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.95 WITHOUT pseudo-transient now converges (442 its; SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 660 its), so the wave-5 premise that plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation than pseudo-transient came from this defect (test now asserts both the legacy failure with h_from_solution = false and the new convergence). Laminar step, parabolic inlet (tests/step_laminar.rs): Re_h = 200 vanLeer SIMPLEC alpha_u 1 + local pseudo cfl 5 converges (607 its); plain SIMPLE/SIMPLEC, linearUpwind and vanLeer converge for Re_h <= 200. STILL NOT MET at Re_h = 400: vanLeer SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (and 0.5/0.2, 0.3/0.1) limit-cycles (residual 0.02-0.2), linearUpwind SIMPLEC 0.95 does not converge (0.4), pseudo local cfl 5 (alpha_u 1) does not converge with vanLeer (4.9e-2) or linearUpwind (4.4e-2) in 3000-4000 its; converging recipes: vanLeer + SIMPLEC alpha_u 0.9 (696 its on 120x16, 1404-2359 its on 320x32 - 480x48) and linearUpwind + SIMPLE 0.7/0.3 (2795 its). So the acceptance (cavity and a step converge with pseudo-transient where plain SIMPLE needs lower relaxation) is only partly met: both converge with pseudo-transient, but plain SIMPLEC now also converges and the Re_h = 400 step still needs a specific scheme/coupling combination. No auto setting beyond the h_from_solution default was added. Laminar reattachment x_r/h (ER 2, parabolic inlet, vanLeer; Re_Armaly = 2 Re_h): Re_h 100: 4.95; 200: 8.19; 389: 11.54; 400: 11.24 / 11.67 / 11.75 on three meshes (not yet mesh independent); remembered literature (NOT verified, from memory): Gartling 1990 Re 800 about 12.2, Armaly 1983 about 12 (3D); lower Re values not citable. Graded step mesh: gen::backward_step_graded (StepGrading, StepSpec::from_expansion_ratio) agrees with the uniform mesh of the same size to 0.2 percent at Re_h 400 (11.70 vs 11.67). Convention warning: Re_h = 389 was run as asked (Re_Armaly 778); Armaly's own '389' would be Re_h about 195, for which Re_h 200 (8.19) is the nearer point.

title: Report definitions, convergence conditions and automatic stopping criteria
acceptance: A report definition (e.g. drag coefficient) can drive a monitor and a stop condition (window range / change tolerance / residual); the run stops automatically and records why
note: P1. Gap: Fluent report definitions, convergence conditions and monitors; CFX convergence conditions and interrupt conditions. Settings tree: top-level convergence.<name> {monitor, type, tolerance, window, relative}; solver.stop_when (any|all), solver.min_iterations. Any monitor can be used: residuals (res_u, res_p, res_T, continuity, courant, dt) or any report (drag coefficient, heat flow, expression report). Reports already feed monitors each iteration/step (F-082); above conditions act as interrupt conditions (run ends with converged=false). The run records why it stopped (Simulation::stop_reason(), status JSON stop_reason, HTML summary row 'Stopped because', CLI prints 'stopped: ...'); built-in reasons: residual targets met, iteration limit, end time. Unknown monitor names are rejected at validation. Measured: lid-driven cavity 12x12 with a lid_drag report, window_range relative tolerance 1e-5 over 10 samples stops after 112 iterations ('range 9.352e-6 <= 1.000e-5'); the window one step earlier did not satisfy it. Tests: 3 unit tests in rcfd-post (window, change/below/above/non-finite, any/all) and 3 case-level tests in rcfd-api (report-driven stop with recorded reason, interrupt + built-in reasons, all-combination). Caveat: conditions are evaluated on recorded monitor samples (once per iteration/step), not on sub-iteration values.

title: Non-Newtonian and temperature-dependent viscosity laws (power, Carreau, Carreau-Yasuda, Cross, Herschel-Bulkley, Bingham; Arrhenius/WLF shift)
acceptance: Power-law channel flow matches the analytic profile; Carreau recovers Newtonian limits at low and high shear; laws exposed in the settings tree with units
note: Done. rcfd-api `rheology`: settings group `rheology` (docs/case-schema.md) with power_law, carreau, carreau_yasuda, cross, herschel_bulkley (Papanastasiou-regularised yield stress) and bingham, viscosity clamps, face-wise relaxation, and temperature dependence by time-temperature superposition mu(g,T) = a_T mu_ref(a_T g) with Arrhenius, WLF or a lookup table a_T(T) (F-105 tables; needs the energy equation). Dynamic viscosities in Pa s, times in s, stress in Pa, declared with units in the schema; the solver uses mu(shear rate sqrt(2 S:S))/rho on the momentum-diffusion faces in steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC (with or without the energy equation) and transient PISO/PIMPLE runs (PimpleSolver gained nu_face). Measured (tests/rheology.rs, checks fixed first, 60x20 plane channel, H=1, U=1, K=0.1): power law n=0.6: profile error 0.77% of centreline (limit 2%), dp/dx +0.26% (limit 3%); n=1.4: 1.15%, -0.86%. Bingham (mu_p 0.1, tau0 0.2, regularisation 200 s) vs Buckingham-Reiner: profile 1.6% of the plug velocity 1.349 (limit 5%), dp/dx +1.04% (limit 5%), 1783 iterations. Carreau, Carreau-Yasuda, Cross and power law (n=1) in their Newtonian limits reproduce the plain run to below 1e-6 (steady and PISO); unit tests: Carreau within 1e-6 of mu_0 at lambda*g=2e-4 and within 3e-3 of mu_inf at 1e14, closed forms, Yasuda a=2 equals Carreau; Arrhenius and table shifts at uniform T equal a Newtonian run with scaled viscosity (1e-6); a temperature outside the shift table stops the run with a message; bad parameters are diagnostics. Law forms are from memory of the literature and marked unverified in docs/reference-data.md. Not done: the transposed-gradient viscous term of a variable viscosity, yield-stress laws with a temperature shift (diagnostic), combination with turbulence models, the compressible solver or a UDF viscosity (diagnostics), restart checkpoints carrying the viscosity relaxation history.

title: Non-conformal mesh interfaces (general grid interface / mortar) with flux conservation
acceptance: Two non-matching blocks give the same channel solution as one conformal block within discretization error; fluxes conserved to round-off across the interface
note: Done (first version, mesh-level). New rcfd-mesh module non_conformal: join_non_conformal(A, patchA, B, patchB, tol) intersects two planar, coplanar, opposed interface patches (Sutherland-Hodgman clipping of convex faces in plane coordinates), emits one ordinary internal face per overlap (owner on the A cell, neighbour on the B cell, area vector = overlap area x normal, centre at the overlap centroid), deletes the original interface faces, merges coincident points and inserts hanging nodes into the in-plane edges of neighbouring faces so every cell stays closed under Mesh::validate. The solver is untouched; flux conservation holds by construction. Case file: mesh.generator = channel_2d_interface (nx/ny, nx_right/ny_right). Checks fixed before running: (1) face overlaps tile each original face and every cell's area vectors close: 20|27 interface 46 overlaps, tiling error 2.8e-15, worst closure 2.9e-17 relative; 3-D 3x4x5 vs 2x7x3 blocks 70 overlaps, tiling 1.0e-15, volume conserved; (2) Poiseuille channel (nu 0.1, interface perpendicular to flow, 20 vs 27 cells across, linear upwind, 2 non-orthogonal correctors): L2 error of u vs exact relative to 1.5: non-conformal 1.93e-3 against conformal 20 cells 2.28e-3 and 27 cells 1.76e-3 (criterion <= 1.5 x the larger, met), max error 6.18e-3 vs 8.08e-3 and 6.18e-3 (met); interface flux 0.100125000000 equals inlet and outlet flux to 2e-16 relative (limit 1e-12); dp/dx -1.2061 vs -1.2 (0.5 percent, limit 2); (3) linear temperature patch test across the interface: max error 7.8e-12 (limit 1e-8). Kernel fix found on the way (affects every case with non-orthogonal correctors): the pressure solve discarded the explicit non-orthogonal term in its first pass and the reported pressure residual excluded it, so res_p stalled at 2e-4 on non-orthogonal meshes; the first pass now uses the gradient of the current pressure and the residual includes the term (converges to 1e-10 in 223 iterations). Not done: non-planar/curved interfaces (rotating-frame sliding/AMI, F-063), partially overlapping interfaces (patches must cover each other), face zones are dropped by the join, transient motion.

title: Interpolate a previous solution onto a new mesh and restart from it

Delivered: rcfd-post interpolate module (nearest source cell by bucket search + least-squares gradient, clipped to the neighbour range; modes nonconservative and conservative), SimpleSolver::set_fields (rebuilds the face flux), Simulation::interpolate_from(source case, checkpoint, mode), rcfd run --interpolate-case/--interpolate-checkpoint/--interpolate-mode, run.headless interpolate_* parameters and matching MCP run_headless fields (docs/run-control.md, docs/service-protocol.md). Measured (checks fixed up front), 12x12 cavity solution onto 24x24: first-iteration normalised residual res_u 0.1656 and res_p 0.1091 versus 1.0 and 1.0 for the uniform start (conservative: 0.1656 and 0.1086); relative L2 distance of the start from the converged speed 0.171 versus 1.000. A linear field is reproduced to 1e-12 inside the source cell-centre hull; conservative mode matches the source volume average of p, ux, uy to 1e-10 (non-conservative differs: ux average 1.43e-3 vs 3.25e-3). Not done: conservative here means a uniform shift that matches the volume average, not a geometric cell-overlap remap (sub-regions are not conserved); the donor cell is the nearest centre, not a point-in-cell search; steady laminar SIMPLE/SIMPLEC only (transient, compressible and turbulence-model state are not interpolated); the source is a checkpoint plus its case, VTU/result files cannot be read back; no GUI control.

The wall-clock limit and stop file are the F-121 controls, verified here on a transient run (stop file -> interrupted/exit 7, --max-elapsed 0 -> time_limit/exit 8). title: glTF/GLB export of surfaces with scalar/vector field colouring for browser and sidebar preview
acceptance: Exported GLB for a contour on a boundary loads in a glTF validator and a viewer with correct colours; size scales linearly with face count
note: Partial (container and content checks pass; external validator and viewer not run). Delivered: rcfd-post gltf module (glb_patches/write_glb, GLB 2.0 with one primitive per boundary patch, flat-shaded viridis COLOR_0 from a cell or face field, raw value in _SCALAR, outward normals, optional fixed colour range), a structural self-check (check_glb: header, chunk alignment, buffer/view/accessor bounds, min/max, index range) and service method render.glb (sandboxed path, optional inline base64). title: Headless launch/run-control contract: batch flags, threads/precision, hostfile, journal playback, check-only, continue/initial-file, state on stdout, control port
acceptance: rcfd run supports check-only, continue-from, interrupt and monitor-state streaming; documented exit codes; a scripted run produces a machine-readable status stream consumed by the MCP server
note: Partial: acceptance met, title scope not. Delivered in rcfd-api `runctl` and `rcfd run`: --check-only, --continue-from/--checkpoint/--checkpoint-every, --stop-file (clean interrupt, exit 7), --max-elapsed (exit 8), --status-json/--status-file/--status-every (rcfd-status v1 JSON lines; stdout carries only events, human text on stderr), --threads, --precision double, --journal playback; documented exit codes 0-8 (docs/run-control.md); same driver behind service run.check/run.headless/status.read and MCP tools check_case_headless, run_headless, read_status_stream (consumes the stream). Measured on a 12x12 cavity (tol 1e-7): uninterrupted 111 iterations; stopped at 40 and continued from the checkpoint also 111 iterations with a byte-identical solution.vtu; 25 steps after a restore bit-identical to 25 uninterrupted steps; --threads 1 vs 4 byte-identical solution.vtu. Not done: --hostfile (rejected, exit 2; needs F-100), single precision (rejected), a control-port socket (remote control is the F-085 service), signal handlers (interrupt via stop file), checkpoints for transient, compressible and turbulence-model runs (steady laminar SIMPLE/SIMPLEC with optional energy only; others warn / fail with exit 1). `rcfd run` now also fails with exit 4 when the mesh quality check fails.

title: User-function plugin API with sandboxed (WASM) execution for sources, BCs, properties and monitors
acceptance: A user-defined momentum source loaded as a WASM module changes the solution as expected; the module cannot access the filesystem or network; the ABI is versioned
note: Done. Sandboxed user functions in rcfd-api `udf` (wasmi 0.31, pure-Rust interpreter; ABI version 1, docs/udf-abi.md): a WebAssembly module must export rcfd_abi_version() and may export momentum_source, velocity_profile, kinematic_viscosity and monitor. Case settings udf.<name> (file, fuel_per_call, momentum_source/viscosity/monitor roles) and boundaries.<patch>.velocity_udf. Isolation: any import (so no WASI, file, network, clock) is refused at load, per-call fuel is renewed on every call and exhaustion traps, linear memory capped at 16 MiB, results must be finite, viscosity positive; failures stop the run with state failed (exit 1), never a panic; module files stay inside the service sandbox root. Measured (tests/udf.rs, checks fixed first): constant momentum_source module equals physics.body_force to below 1e-9 relative and differs from a run without it; kinematic_viscosity module and velocity_profile module reproduce the plain physics.nu / expression runs to below 1e-9; monitor equals the independent sum(ux*V) to 1e-12; infinite loop, memory growth past the cap, NaN, negative viscosity, wrong ABI, wrong signature, missing ABI export and imports (wasi fd_write) are all rejected; 20000 calls under a 1000-fuel budget succeed. Position-dependent source a=(3x,0,0) in a closed 10x10 box: first check (max|u|<1e-6) measured 4.4e-2 because the wall pressure extrapolation uses the owner-cell force (first order for non-uniform forces), so it was replaced, not loosened, by a convergence check written before the 20x20 run: spurious velocity 4.44e-2 -> 1.09e-2 (ratio 4.1), pressure error 3.86e-2 -> 1.94e-2 (ratio 2.0), both above the 1.7 floor. Not done: momentum source and viscosity in transient runs (refused), anything in the compressible solver (refused), viscosity together with a turbulence model (refused), scalar/energy sources, host functions, batch interface (every cell is one interpreted call), no MCP or assistant tool wrapper for udf settings (settings are available through the generic case tools and schema).
